mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter credit conditions and reduced corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during Fed rate hikes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or Fed Funds Rate does not exceed 4.0% in any month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.2 percentage points over three consecutive months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightening reduces wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by ≥0.2pp month-on-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE rises ≥0.2pp for 3 months, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the pattern persists for >6 months without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household spending index) exceeds 600 for two consecutive months, it predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong consumer demand supports corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: During such demand spikes, 20-day forward returns are negative or flat (mean return ≤ 0), or the pattern is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% followed by a rebound of ≥3% in the next month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as a classic supply shock lowers earnings growth forecasts.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥2% then rises ≥3% in consecutive months
failure_condition: The pattern occurs but 20-day forward returns remain positive or unchanged, or the shock is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining CPIAUCSL (CPI) by at least 0.3% each month are associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate future inflation pressures and rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such inflation declines, 5-day forward returns are not negative or the pattern is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 5,000 in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness can signal softening demand and lower wage growth risks.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by ≥5,000 in a single month
failure_condition: In such episodes, forward returns are not positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private demand) grows faster than monthly CPIAUCSL (CPI) by at least 1%, it indicates a shift toward real demand strength and predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥1% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the positive return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or the relative growth condition does not hold for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to rising RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 10% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a supply-side recovery and is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by ≥10% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply recovery, forward returns are not positive or the pattern is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
